scope: synthetic sensor anomaly database idempotency and actual EventBus receipt recovery after worker hard exit

verification.schema_scope: Focused prerequisite schemas plus direct application of 081_oracle_infrastructure.sql, 116_event_bus.sql, 165_event_bus_durability.sql, 334_ingestion_validation_provenance.sql, 375_notification_outbox.sql, and 376_sensor_anomaly_delivery.sql. The complete repository migration and seed set was not applied.
checks: a child process runs the actual EventBus worker and hard-exits with code 86 after the sensor_reading handler transaction commits but before receipt acknowledgement
the source event lease is expired and a replacement EventBus worker reclaims the event and completes delivery on attempt two
notification_outbox.source_event_id matches the preallocated sensor_alert platform event ID
actual worker retry preserves exactly one sensor_alert, draft mrv_claim, sensor_anomaly_effect, ingestion_log row, follow-up platform_event, and actuation_log record
actual worker retry preserves exactly three notification intents: webhook, Directus, and email
delivery receipt remains processing at attempt one after crash, then succeeds at attempt two with one success handler log
critical actuation remains requires_approval with human_approval_required=true and no approver
persisted notification payloads contain no SMTP host, SMTP credentials, Directus token, or configured email recipient
fake SMTP send uses an outbox-derived Message-ID and X-Kokonut-Idempotency-Key
no notification delivery worker, real provider endpoint, or actuator was invoked
network has internal=true and no published ports

source_validation.compose_config: passed for candidate, candidate plus standard, portability, and sensor-recovery manifests
passed for candidate, standard, portability, and sensor-recovery manifests

limitations: The fixture used focused schemas and synthetic rows, not the complete repository migration set or a populated farm database.

SMTP/Directus/webhook provider acceptance, receiver-side deduplication, retention ownership, operator authorization, recovery coverage for additional handlers/runtime conditions, and broader CAP-040 acceptance remain open.
Migrations 375 and 376 were not applied to the candidate or legacy application databases.
